PullRequest.Title: Cache API Scan dependencies in official builds
PullRequest.Body:
Caches the dedicated API Scan `node_modules` tree so subsequent Windows x64 official builds can avoid the approximately 13-minute dependency installation.

The cache remains separate from the regular Windows build dependency cache because API Scan configures native builds with `/Zi`, `/FS`, and `/profile` to produce scan symbols. Its identity includes dependency metadata, architecture, process architecture, the generated GYP configuration, and the selected npm registry.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The ordering is explicit in the changed YAML, the restored archive explicitly contains all node_modules files, and the invoked script explicitly performs an unpruned sequential recursive filesystem walk. Only the exact elapsed-time magnitude varies with dependency-tree size and agent filesystem performance.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Sequential filesystem readdir/stat operations over the extracted node_modules trees, plus rewrites of nested package-lock files
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On every warm API Scan build, cost grows with the total number of files and directories in all cached node_modules trees rather than only the checked-out source tree; setup-npm-registry.ts awaits a stat for each entry and recursively descends without excluding node_modules.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased warm-build latency and excessive filesystem I/O on the API Scan critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The registry setup ran immediately after checkout/key-vault setup, before npm ci, so its recursive package-lock search traversed the source checkout while no dependency trees existed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The moved setup step now runs after Cache@2 restoration and 7z extraction, so a cache hit places every cached node_modules tree under the recursive search root before it starts.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The diff deletes the Setup NPM Registry task from before include.gypi/cache handling and re-adds it at RIGHT line 77, after RIGHT line 73 extracts .build/apiscan_node_modules_cache/cache.7z into the checkout.
Findings.Title: Run registry setup before extracting the dependency cache
Findings.Impact: Each official Windows x64 API Scan cache hit can perform a sequential metadata walk over the entire restored dependency forest before compilation, eroding the intended dependency-cache latency savings; large dependency trees make this potentially minutes of Windows filesystem work.
Findings.Evidence: Added line 77 invokes build/setup-npm-registry.ts after the added cache extraction at line 73. That script's getPackageLockFiles recursively calls readdir for every directory and awaits fs.stat for every entry with no node_modules pruning. The cache archive is built from listNodeModules.ts, which enumerates files from every node_modules tree across the repository, so the warm path guarantees a much larger traversal than the pre-diff placement.
Findings.Recommendation: Move the Setup NPM Registry task back before cache extraction (the cache key already includes NPM_REGISTRY), or make setup-npm-registry.ts explicitly prune node_modules for this invocation so only repository lockfiles are visited.

Scenarios.Scenario: Official Windows x64 API Scan dependency preparation, on cold and warm node_modules cache paths
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkout and tool setup precede key generation. A warm run must download and extract the cache, then currently complete the recursively expanded registry rewrite, Foundry validation/install, optional-dependency check, quality mixins, compilation, symbol download, and API Scan. A cold run performs npm ci, distro mixin, full dependency-tree enumeration/compression, then continues to compilation; cache upload is handled by Cache@2 after the job rather than gating compilation, but archive creation itself is on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cache@2 downloads the compressed API Scan dependency archive on an exact hit and uploads a newly created archive after a miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cache restore and, only for a new key, one post-job save per API Scan job; transfer bytes scale with the compressed aggregate node_modules tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No dependency cache transfer occurred; every API Scan job proceeded to npm ci.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restore/download must finish before extraction and compilation. Save is post-job, while local archive construction is earlier on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: 7z extracts the full cached node_modules archive into the checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One process on a warm exact hit; filesystem writes scale with every archived dependency file and total uncompressed bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No archive extraction occurred; npm ci materialized dependencies instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extraction blocks all subsequent dependency preparation and compilation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: setup-npm-registry.ts recursively enumerates directories, stats each entry, and rewrites every discovered package-lock.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation per configured-registry job, but on a warm hit it issues sequential operations for every source and restored node_modules entry, including all nested dependency trees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same invocation ran before dependencies existed and traversed only the source checkout; the diff moved it after cache extraction and materially amplified its filesystem cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The complete recursive walk blocks Foundry setup, compilation, and API Scan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: npm ci resolves/downloads and installs all repository dependencies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One npm invocation on a cold miss, internally covering the dependency graph; zero on an exact cache hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ran on every API Scan job; the diff preserves it on misses and removes it from warm hits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the cold path before compilation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Foundry Local lifecycle installation validates and fetches required native libraries, with skipIfPresent for already materialized cached artifacts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lifecycle invocation per job; artifact network fetches occur only for required libraries absent locally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prepare/install templates already ran on every API Scan job before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously before compilation. On a valid warm archive, library downloads are avoided by presence checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: checkNativeOptionalDeps.ts performs presence checks for two native optional dependency package pairs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A constant number of path-existence checks per job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This validation was absent from the API Scan job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before compilation but has bounded negligible I/O.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: listNodeModules.ts enumerates every dependency file and 7z compresses those files into the cache archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-tree enumeration and one compression process per cold cache key; work and output bytes scale with aggregate node_modules file count and size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: After npm ci the job went directly to quality mixin and compilation without enumerating/compressing the dependency forest.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Archive creation blocks the cold job before compilation, although the resulting Cache@2 upload occurs after the job. This is intentional miss-path work amortized by later hits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing downstream steps download symbols, invoke API Scan services, and publish symbols/security logs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One compile/symbol/API Scan/publish sequence for the single x64 job, with artifact bytes determined by the build output.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same downstream boundaries and ordering existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These remain downstream of dependency preparation and are unchanged; dependency-path delays postpone them but do not alter their call count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One API Scan job per official build. Effective dependency cardinality is the aggregate file/directory count across repository-root, build, remote, extension, and test node_modules trees; cache transfer/compression scales with their total bytes. The registry search is not grouped or pruned and therefore visits every restored entry on a warm hit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pipeline steps are serialized. setup-npm-registry.ts recursively awaits each readdir/stat operation, so its per-entry filesystem fan-out has effective concurrency of one. npm ci is one process with npm-managed fetch concurrency; 7z is one extraction or compression process; there is no cross-build request coalescing beyond the immutable shared cache key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cache key hashes the repository npm metadata, target/host architecture, API-scan marker, deterministic GYP configuration hash, and selected registry. There are no restore keys or partial matches. A cold miss installs and archives the full tree for later immutable-cache upload. A warm exact hit downloads/extracts the archive and skips npm ci plus distro mixin/archive creation, but the moved registry setup then scans the restored dependency tree. Foundry's native-library fetch uses skipIfPresent on cached files; there is no negative-cache path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: YAML ordering proves extraction precedes the moved registry task; the archive generator proves all node_modules files are restored; and setup-npm-registry.ts proves an unpruned, sequential recursive filesystem walk.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The repository structure proves the warm traversal's cardinality increase, but exact file count, Windows metadata latency, compression duration, cache size, and net end-to-end savings are not measured in the diff. This uncertainty supports medium rather than high severity for the reported regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: One reportable warm-cache boundary-fanout regression: moving registry setup after extraction causes a sequential walk of the full restored dependency forest. The added warm restore otherwise replaces the prior npm ci boundary, and cold archive creation is a bounded, intentional cache-population tradeoff rather than a separate regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed pipeline file and traced the API Scan job's warm/cold cache lifecycle, subprocesses, filesystem walks, network operations, cache key, cardinality, and serialization. Submitted one medium-severity finding for the diff-amplified recursive registry scan on warm cache hits; no regression-fix learning record was justified because the prior uncached install was not proven to be a shipped regression with an identifiable introducing change.
